newsitem.title: LATVIA: Leading Latvian bank Unibanka doubles '96 profit.
newsitem.headline: Leading Latvian bank Unibanka doubles '96 profit.

text.p: One of Latvia's leading banks Unibanka on Monday said it made an audited profit after tax in 1996 of 5.978 million lats versus 3.024 million in the previous year.
The bank said in a statement giving the main elements of its audited earnings that assets in 1996 rose to 149.735 million lats from 115.167 million.

Unibanka, a former state-owned bank, is now one of the leading shares on the Latvian bourse and has the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) and Swedish Swedfund as two key foreign investors.
The Latvian state now owns a minority 33 percent.
"Unibanka's business in 1996 took place as the economy as a whole stabilised to a certain extent and got over the 1995 banking crisis," Unibanka said in a statement.
Latvia in 1995 was hit by one of the worst banking crises in eastern Europe when was its largest bank, Banka Baltija, collapsed.
Unibanka said its deposits rose in 1996 by 52 percent but did not give a figure for deposits while loans extended rose by 30 percent to 46 million lats.
It said that bad and doubtful loans were just two percent of the loan portfolio, which it said was within European standards.
The bank said that its own capital rose last year to 26 million lats from 14 million lats.

Unibanka said that the profit per Unibanka share was 34 santimes last year and that it would pay a certain amount of the profit back to shareholders as a dividend. However, it said most of the profit would be distributed in the form of new shares.
